title: Fracture Protocol
brief: Original-IP fps game (sub-genre: fps). Capture the core mechanics and game-feel of "Half-Life 2" (critically acclaimed, 96%) — but with your OWN original name, theme, characters and art. Do NOT reference or reuse that title's IP. SIGNATURE MECHANIC for this genre: . MUST SHIP COMPLETE: a working menu (title + difficulty + how-to + settings via FFG.Shell), the page control bar (fullscreen/mute/pause), a clear win AND lose state, readable HUD, and polished feel — it must play start-to-finish with no manual fixes.

M0.done_when: design doc written: core loop, verbs, scope, art direction, definition_of_done

M1.done_when: core loop genuinely playable in ONE level: structure+feel green, no crash

M2.done_when: every verb in the design doc implemented and survives the play-bot

M3.done_when: multiple levels + progression + a real difficulty curve; everything reachable

M4.done_when: menu + audio + game-feel/juice; vision fidelity high; zero crashes

M5.done_when: deep QA: structure+feel+fidelity+review all green across repeated playthroughs

design_doc.title: Fracture Protocol
design_doc.core_loop: You are Dr. Kira Voss, a physicist trapped in the ruins of Meridian Station after a catastrophic experiment tears reality apart. Navigate interconnected industrial zones and research labs, wielding improvised tools and experimental weaponry scavenged from the wreckage. Solve environmental physics puzzles using the Rift Manipulatorâ€”a device that lets you grab, hurl, and redirect objects and energy streamsâ€”while fighting hostile security drones and reality-warped entities. Progress through linear-but-exploratory levels, alternating between quiet puzzle-solving, tense combat encounters, and narrative-driven setpieces that reveal the station's dark secrets.

in_v1: 5 linear levels (industrial corridor, flooded labs, gravity-anomaly sector, server farm, reactor core)
Rift Manipulator: grab/throw/rotate physics objects, redirect laser beams, pull/push weighted objects
4 weapons: pulse pistol, scatter rifle, arc launcher, frag grenades
3 enemy types: security drones (hitscan), corrupted workers (melee rush), rift anomalies (projectile spam)
Physics puzzles: stacking crates to climb, redirecting power conduits, building bridges with debris, blocking laser grids
Narrative: environmental storytelling via audio logs, terminal readouts, environmental detailsâ€”no cutscenes
Boss fight: corrupted AI core at reactor level requiring puzzle-combat hybrid
HUD: health, ammo, manipulator charge, objective marker, crosshair
Menu: title screen, difficulty (easy/normal/hard affects damage/enemy aggression), settings (volume, sensitivity), how-to-play screen with control diagram
Win state: reactor shutdown + escape timer success
Lose state: death triggers respawn at last checkpoint or restart level
out_v1: No open-world or branching pathsâ€”strictly linear progression
No inventory system or resource crafting
No character customization or skill trees
No dialogue trees or player choice in narrative

design_doc.art_direction: Industrial sci-fi decay. Palette: cold steel grays, rust oranges, sickly acid greens (rift energy), deep shadow blacks with high-contrast emergency lighting (red alarms, flickering fluorescents). Mood: claustrophobic dread meets silent-protagonist resilience. Environments show layered historyâ€”pre-disaster sterile labs covered in debris, broken glass, sparking wires, and reality distortions (floating debris, inverted gravity zones, glitching textures). Minimalist UI in neon cyan overlays. Weapon designs: chunky, utilitarian, clearly cobbled-together tech. Enemy silhouettes instantly readableâ€”drones are angular/metallic, workers shamble and twitch, anomalies glow and warp space around them.

milestone_plan.M1: Vertical slice: 1 complete level (industrial corridor) with Rift Manipulator core mechanic, 1 weapon (pulse pistol), 1 enemy type (drones), 2 physics puzzles (stack crates to reach vent, redirect laser to unlock door), working HUD, menu with FFG.Shell integration, death/respawn, and level-complete trigger. Prove the manipulator feel is satisfying and combat-puzzle pacing works.
milestone_plan.M2: All 5 levels blocked out with placeholder art, all 4 weapons implemented and balanced, all 3 enemy types spawning with basic AI behaviors (patrol, chase, attack patterns), manipulator can grab/throw/rotate/pull/push with charge meter, checkpoint system saves progress within levels, audio logs placed for narrative beats.
milestone_plan.M3: All levels fully art-passed with environmental storytelling details, boss fight scripted and tuned, all physics puzzles final and playtested for solution clarity, difficulty modes affect enemy damage/health/aggression, settings menu controls audio/input sensitivity, how-to-play screen shows all verbs with controller/keyboard diagrams, win-state escape sequence with countdown timer, lose-state game-over screen with retry options.
milestone_plan.M4: Polish pass: particle effects for weapon impacts and rift energy, screen shake and camera recoil, sound design for all weapons/enemies/manipulator, ambient audio (alarms, dripping water, distant machinery), lighting pass for mood and readability, UI animations (health damage flash, ammo counter updates, objective pings), tutorial prompts for first use of each mechanic, balance pass based on internal playtest (5+ runs on each difficulty).
milestone_plan.M5: Ship-ready: all FFG.Shell requirements met (title screen, difficulty select, settings persist, how-to-play accessible from pause menu), page control bar (fullscreen toggle, mute, pause), performance optimization (stable 60fps target), final bug triage (no soft-locks, all checkpoints fire, all win/lose states trigger reliably), credits screen, build tested on target platforms (Windows/WebGL), trailer-ready gameplay capture, itch.io page assets prepared.

definition_of_done: Player can launch game, see title screen, select difficulty, view how-to-play, adjust settings (volume/sensitivity), and start level 1 without errors.
All 5 levels can be completed start-to-finish on all difficulty modes without soft-locks or game-breaking bugs.
Rift Manipulator can grab/throw/rotate at least 10 unique physics objects per level; player can solve every puzzle using manipulator verbs.
All 4 weapons have distinct feel, sound, particle effects, and ammo economy; player can switch weapons mid-combat smoothly.
All 3 enemy types spawn, patrol, detect player, attack with unique behaviors, take damage with visual feedback, and die with ragdoll/destruction effects.
Boss fight requires both combat (damaging weak points) and puzzle-solving (manipulator to expose weak points); clear win condition when boss defeated.
HUD always displays current health, ammo for equipped weapon, manipulator charge, and objective marker pointing to next goal.
Death triggers respawn at last checkpoint or level restart; checkpoints auto-save and are clearly marked in-world.
Win state: final boss defeated, reactor shutdown sequence completes, escape timer counts down, player reaches extraction zone, victory screen displays with time/difficulty.
Lose state: player health reaches zero OR escape timer expires, game-over screen offers retry from checkpoint or return to main menu.
FFG.Shell menu accessible from pause menu; fullscreen/mute/pause controls on page control bar work at all times.
Performance: maintains 60fps on mid-tier hardware (or WebGL equivalent), no stuttering during physics-heavy scenes.
Audio: all weapons, enemies, manipulator actions, environmental ambience, and UI interactions have sound effects; audio logs play clearly and pause combat music.

Narrative: at least 15 audio logs collectible across 5 levels, terminal readouts provide context for station disaster, environmental details (blood trails, scattered notes, warning signs) tell story without text dumps.
Accessibility: subtitles for all audio logs, colorblind-friendly UI elements, adjustable crosshair size, key rebinding in settings.
No placeholder assets in shipped build: all textures, models, sounds are final or temp-but-cohesive; no missing textures or silent audio cues.
Build launches on Windows and WebGL without manual fixes; itch.io embed works full-screen with no black-screen bugs.
Credits screen lists all tools, assets, inspirations; links to ForgeFlow Games and sequel teaser (if applicable).
